All procedural claims are jurisdiction-qualified ('most states', 'many jurisdictions', 'most courts') or attributed to constitutional precedent ('established by the Supreme Court as a constitutional due process requirement'). No bare universal deadlines or filing requirements.
No case citations appear anywhere in the post. Constitutional rights are attributed to 'the Supreme Court' generally without citing specific case names.
Post references employment, housing, and family stability only as things to 'preserve' during the process — no universal collateral-consequence claims like license loss or voting rights appear.
